summary: Lookout tower named Banks in Bradley County; the town of Banks lies about 3.5 miles southwest of it. Only a directory listing and a map site name it; no agency, date, status or access found.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists a Banks lookout in Bradley County
map site names Banks Lookout Tower in Clay Township
evidence.quote: Banks Lookout Tower is a tower in Clay Township

evidence.supports: town of Banks lies about 3.5 miles southwest of the tower
evidence.quote: Banks is situated 3½ miles southwest of Banks Lookout Tower.

evidence.supports: town once known for ties to railroads and timber
evidence.quote: Once known for its relationship to the railroads and the timber industry

evidence.supports: James E. Lindsay of Davenport, Iowa, was an investor in the area
evidence.quote: James E. Lindsay of Davenport, Iowa, was one of the investors drawn to the area.

evidence.supports: company acquired land in 1883 at the location that became Banks
evidence.quote: His company, Lindsay Land and Lumber, acquired property in 1883 at the location that would become Banks.
For reasons no longer remembered, the post office changed its name in 1906 to Banks.
The next year, the town of Banks was incorporated.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record. The Forest Lookouts Banks page holds only the name and 'Bradley County'; it names no agency, designation, height, build date or status. Mapcarta is a crowd-sourced map that confirms the tower's name and gives its position relative to the town. The Encyclopedia of Arkansas Banks entry covers the town and does not mention a lookout. The story sits below the 120-word floor because the sources give nothing more on the tower; it is kept short rather than padded. Brief checks: county and coordinates agree with the Forest Lookouts page; the brief's agency is null and stays unknown. No corrections. The town-history sentences (1883, 1906, 1907) are supported by the Encyclopedia of Arkansas evidence but kept out of events, which record the lookout only.
